_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla, typed out on the slip. Each lesson has two: "start" comes on as the lesson opens, and "check" is a short quiz once the lesson's check is done. Each talk has turns; in each turn Walla Walla says "them" and the player picks one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."). A reply can have a "back" line, and "right": true marks the right answer to a question (it is never scored). Every reply leads on to the next turn. This is the opening talk, heard once on the home page; a reply with "off": true switches the radio off.

turns.them: CQ, CQ, CQ. This is W7DQ, Walla Walla, calling the new station at Harrow. Anybody up there, or did the wind carry you off to Idaho? Come back.

replies.say: W7DQ, this is W7HAR, Harrow. I’m here. I think.
replies.back: Fine signal. You sound about twelve years old, but that may be the static.
It’s on, and so is half of Adams County. Give your call sign, tenderfoot.
Suspicious. I like that in a weather forecaster. W7DQ, Walla Walla. I’ve been reading skies down here since before you were born.

turns.them: Here’s the arrangement, as the Bureau explained it to me in a letter with too many carbon copies. You’re the new forecaster at Harrow, and a workbook comes up on the train, a lesson at a time. I’ll get on the air as you start each one, and quiz you when you finish it.

replies.back: Like school, only the bell is a thunderstorm.

turns.them: One more thing. If you’d rather study in peace, say so, and I’ll keep off the air.

replies.say: Keep the radio on. I’ll want the help.
replies.back: Splendid. Seventy-three: that’s ham for best regards.
Suit yourself. If you change your mind, the dial is in Settings.
